headline: Divestiture charge masks strong underlying profit growth
summary_short: Hormel reported Q2 FY2026 net sales of $2.97 billion, up 2.5% y/y (organic +3%), and GAAP diluted EPS of $0.29, down 12.1% y/y on a $61 million loss from the divested whole-bird turkey business. Adjusted diluted EPS of $0.40 rose 14.3% y/y.
summary_long: GAAP diluted EPS fell 12.1% y/y to $0.29 on a $61M loss from the divested whole-bird turkey business; adjusted diluted EPS rose 14.3% to $0.40 — the sixth straight quarter of organic net-sales growth. Net sales rose 2.5% to $2.97B (organic +3%): Foodservice (+6% sales, +11% profit) and International (+4% sales, +20% profit) offset flat Retail. Operating income fell 12.6% to $217M on the divestiture charge; adjusted operating margin expanded to 9.9% from 9.1%. Cash from operations was $179M; cash rose $156M since fiscal year-end to $827M. FY2026 GAAP EPS guidance was lowered to $1.28-$1.37 (from $1.37-$1.46) to reflect the loss, while adjusted EPS guidance of $1.43-$1.51 was reaffirmed.

drivers.explanation: Organic net sales rose 3%, with Foodservice (+7% organic) and International (+5% organic) growth offsetting a Retail organic-volume decline tied to exiting non-core private-label snack-nut items.
GAAP operating income fell mainly on a $61 million loss from the whole-bird turkey business sale plus higher SG&A; adjusted operating margin still expanded to 9.9% from 9.1%.
GAAP net income declined primarily on the turkey-business divestiture loss and a higher effective tax rate (23.6% vs 22.0%), partially offset by higher segment profit.
Each segment grew both net sales and segment profit; management cited the sixth consecutive quarter of organic top-line growth and confidence in the full-year outlook.
